thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency SLO breach detected on /v1/generate-stream (region: us-west-2). p95=1.25s (SLO=500ms), p99=4.8s (SLO=2s), streaming stalls observed. Affected pool: shared-gpu-pool-3. Auto-mitigation not triggered (threshold=30m). Paging oncall now.

Amy S.: Ack, I'm oncall. Pulling dashboards.

Paul T.: I'm nearby, can help with migrations if needed.

Amy S.: Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abcd1234/streaming-latency?orgId=1 (p95 spike at 02:09 UTC, tail rising since 02:02).

Sam R.: Checking host metrics. Getting sustained GPU PCIe write stalls on hosts hgp-03 and hgp-07. NVMe write queue depth also spiking. Might be IO-bound noisy neighbor.

Miguel (infra): Confirmed. dstat and iostat show heavy nvme_smart writes from tenant-7712 on hgp-07.

Amy S.: Quick customer impact check — Jordan can you pull active tenants list for pool-3 in last 10m?

Jordan (CS): Pulling now. Looks like 6 customers had streaming traffic: tenant-7712 (high throughput), tenant-4321 (moderate), tenant-9000 (low). Customer-facing symptoms reported: increased token latencies and intermittent partial streams (clients see stalled chunks). No new support tickets yet but one customer reported degraded UX.

Paul T.: Running cgroup snapshot for the tenant processes on hgp-07:

```
$ sudo cgget -g blkio:/redwood/tenant-7712
blkio.throttle.read_bps_device: 8:0 0
blkio.throttle.write_bps_device: 8:0 0
blkio.throttle.read_iops_device: 8:0 0
blkio.throttle.write_iops_device: 8:0 0
cpu.stat: usage_usec 8234123
```

Sam R.: Looks like we haven't enforced blkio QoS for that tenant, so it's hammering NVMe. Also KV cache eviction shocks are visible: model kv cache miss rate spiked to 45% which amplifies token processing cost.

Amy S.: Immediate mitigation options: 1) apply temporary blkio limit to tenant-7712, 2) migrate tenant to dedicated pool, 3) evict and restart the tenant containers on affected hosts, 4) burst new dedicated nodes. I can try #1 and #3 now. Any objections?

Paul T.: Go for #1 first. Use conservative limits so we don't starve tenant but reduce noise. If no improvement in 5m, then evict.

Miguel (infra): I'll prepare migration flags and a dedicated pool; ETA ~10m to spin up 2 p4d-like instances and attach model weights.

Amy S.: Applying blkio limits now:

```
$ sudo cgset -r blkio.throttle.write_bps_device="8:0 20000000" /redwood/tenant-7712
$ sudo cgset -r blkio.throttle.read_bps_device="8:0 20000000" /redwood/tenant-7712
```

Amy S.: Applied. Monitoring...

(1 minute later)

Amy S.: p95 dropped from 1.25s -> 0.68s, p99 down to 2.9s. Streaming stalls reduced but still present for some long sequences.

Jordan (CS): Customer 7712 reported partial recovery, they still see occasional stalls on >5k token sequences.

Sam R.: KV cache shows gradual refill. Host hgp-07 IO queue depth dropped ~60%. Good sign.

Amy S.: Let's do graceful eviction for tenant-7712 on hgp-07 and hgp-03 to further reduce tail. We'll reschedule them onto less busy hosts in the shared pool while infra brings up dedicated instances. Initiating eviction: `redwood tenant migrate --tenant 7712 --from-host hgp-07 --to-host spare-12`

Paul T.: I'll monitor for bond/reconnect errors. Also increasing async batching threshold for streaming on those hosts to reduce per-token pressure.

(5 minutes later)

Amy S.: Migration completed for tenant-7712 to spare-12, p95=0.52s, p99=1.9s, stalls largely cleared. KV cache hit rate returning to baseline.

Miguel (infra): Dedicated nodes are up and warming weights. If we want to move 7712 off shared entirely, we can cutover in ~7m.

Jordan (CS): CS contacted tenant-4321 proactively to warn of potential transient latency and offer dedicated instance if needed. Tenant-9000 unaffected.

Amy S.: Customer impact summary for postmortem: tenant-7712 experienced degraded streaming (stalls & elevated p99) for ~22 minutes; ~8% of their streamed requests saw partial stalls. Other tenants saw minor p95 blips but no user-facing failures. No SLA credit likely required but CS will follow up.

Paul T.: Root cause hypothesis: tenant-7712 ran an NVMe-heavy workload (large batched checkpoints + streaming) which wasn't limited by blkio cgroup; multi-tenant GPU hosts saw IO-induced tail latency causing KV cache evictions and higher per-token compute latency.

Amy S.: Mitigations and follow-ups:
- Enforce default blkio limits on shared-gpu-pools (rollout policy)
- Add automatic noisy-tenant detection (nvme/ioop thresholds) to incident-bot for proactive throttling
- Improve KV cache prefetch heuristics to reduce eviction amplification from IO spikes
- Add a migration playbook for noisy tenants to move to dedicated pools quickly
- Post-incident customer comms draft (Jordan)

Sam R.: I'll file infra tasks: BLKIO-2026 (rollout default limits), MIGRATE-2026 (fast path for tenant migration), KV-2026 (prefetch tuning).

Amy S.: Handoff to next oncall (Sam R.) for monitoring through cooldown window (30m). Leaving logs and commands in thread.

Sam R.: Ack, taking over monitoring. If we see another spike, escalate to infra with immediate eviction permission.

Night-Ops Bot: incident-bot auto-note: incident created INC-2026-5329991, severity: P2, status: mitigated -> monitoring.

Amy S.: Thanks team. I'll draft the incident summary and include the timeline, mitigation commands, and customer impact for the postmortem. Jordan will coordinate customer outreach.

Jordan (CS): Draft ready, will send note to tenant-7712 with apology + offer of dedicated capacity trial.

Sam R.: Closing handoff at 03:20 UTC, monitoring until 03:50.

(Last check)

Sam R.: p95=0.48s, p99=1.7s, no new stalls in last 10m. Marking incident as resolved for oncall.

Amy S.: Great work everyone :thumbsup:
